title: Sports Edge Lab · NFL
slate_intro: All 11 Sunday games, plus Monday for the complete Circa board. There are no NFL games on Saturday, November 21. The default outlook uses the strongest usable saved matchup snapshot, with its original November 16 inputs clearly dated.
winner_target_label: Outright win probability; ties remain separate

T120.label: T120 usable snapshot
T120.description: Prices observed Nov 16; projections compiled Nov 16 at 2:14 p.m. PT. These models remained selected in the Nov 18–19 R18 return. This is a dated early outlook, not a current-price refresh.

T60.label: T60 audit · unavailable
T60.description: The latest T60 future rows lack qualified current winner prices. Several selected policies return constant outputs across the slate. Current matchup forecasts are unavailable; retrospective model scores remain visible under Model leaders.

performance_note: The November 22 research compares new two-hour and one-hour quantile models with the prior leaders registered in the N162 fit program. The 2024 and 2025 annual scores each count for half. The 2026 games were graded after selection.
The earlier R18 cards use their own historical registry. The R20 and N164 sections keep their original comparison populations and dates. The weekly outlook uses its November 16 forecast inputs.
performance_method: Primary validation = 0.5 × the 2024 annual metric + 0.5 × the 2025 annual metric. Every winner, margin and total objective has its own selected model; no single overall champion is assumed.

Binary winner metrics exclude actual ties and renormalize home/away probabilities. Displayed matchup probabilities retain a separate tie category. Binary game counts are 285 / 284 / 149 for 2024 / 2025 / 2026; point-error counts are 285 / 285 / 150.
MAE is average absolute point error. RMSE takes the square root within each season before the 50/50 annual blend. Lower error, log loss and Brier scores are better; higher winner accuracy is better.
T60 and T120 are different information-clock groups. Compare a contender with its own clock’s incumbent. T120’s smaller validation score is not proof that changing the horizon causes an improvement.
Three T60 winner-accuracy nominees tie on validation. All remain co-leaders; one has an unavailable 2026 regrade. No 2026 result was used to resolve that tie.
The R20 comparison reads existing, hash-verified predictions. It performed zero estimator fits, did not alter official rankings, and did not launch the unfinished research campaign.

newest_model_comparison.validation: Equal weight to2024 and2025 annual metrics; no2026 selection
newest_model_comparison.future_evidence: Conditional future fixtures using scheduled future origin, not original issued current forecasts
newest_model_comparison.comparison_qualification: Same horizon and exact full-season games. Model families and inputs differ; this is comparative performance, not a controlled causal ablation. Prior test exposure remains disclosed.

circa_deadline.label: ENTRY DEADLINE · SAT NOV 21 · 4:00 PM PT

circa_source_summary: Official Week 11 contest lines, verified November 20. Cover probabilities use the preserved November 16 T120 distribution and are a dated research comparison at these exact lines.
circa_note: Choose five distinct games, one side per game. Win = 1 point, push = 0.5, loss = 0. Totals are not Circa Million entries.
circa_method: The official Circa Million VIII Week 11 sheet determines the contest spreads. All 24 remaining sides are included. The completed Thursday game is excluded.
The entry deadline is Saturday, November 21 at 4:00 p.m. Pacific. A contest card uses exactly five different games, with one side per game.
Expected contest points = P(cover) + 0.5 × P(push). A five-game expectation is the sum of its five individual expectations; independence is not required for that sum.
Probabilities must come from the saved integer-margin distribution evaluated at the official line. The outright win probability and the projected margin alone are not cover probabilities.

The saved integer margin grid runs from −100 to +100, in one-point steps, with away-minus-home orientation. Its probabilities reproduce the source win/tie values within 6.1e−13. No normal approximation, new fit, reconstructed distribution or renormalization is used.

The primary Circa role is the T120 spread-Brier and spread-log-loss selection. The accuracy-selected policy is retained as a separate comparison in the public evidence. Neither role receives a fresh 2026 regrade here.

These are exact evaluations of the saved November 16 conditional margin distributions at the official Week 11 contest lines. Prices, injuries and model inputs have not been refreshed. This is an early conditional card, not a newly issued forecast.
source_summary: Weekly forecast inputs were observed November 16. The R18 evaluation was verified November 18–19, the archived R20 comparison and original contest-line review on November 20, and the quantile research and reconstructed contest grades on November 22.
notes: All dates and kickoff times use America/Los_Angeles. Minnesota–San Francisco is in Mexico City; San Francisco is the designated home team.
Forecast issue, compilation, market observation, selection and dashboard publication are separate clocks. No original live T60 issue is claimed for the conditional future rows.
Probability, projected margin and projected total use separate objective-selected policies. Implied scores from combining margin and total would be a synthesis, not a single joint score forecast.
Only selected rounded forecast values, aggregate performance and public role aliases are published. Historical releases remain available as dated evidence.
